## Enumerated constants

### `entasis_distance_query_state_t`

tolerance-bounded geometry state

| Constant                        | Value | Meaning                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_UNRESOLVED`   |   `0` | no valid geometric result. inspect the returned status            |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_SEPARATED`    |   `1` | positive distance with closest witnesses                          |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_INTERSECTING` |   `2` | zero distance. distance alone does not determine a unique normal  |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_TOUCHING`     |   `3` | touching within the query tolerance. zero correction              |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_PENETRATING`  |   `4` | positive convex separating depth or verified composite correction |

### `entasis_distance_query_kind_t`

operation in the dedicated distance batch, independent of the older query union

| Constant                               | Value | Meaning                                                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ----: | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_QUERY_CLOSEST_POINT` |   `0` | use point and shape_b/pose_b                                       |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_QUERY_DISTANCE`      |   `1` | closest witnesses between supported shapes                         |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_QUERY_PENETRATION`   |   `2` | fixed-orientation convex minimum separating translation            |
| `ENTASIS_DISTANCE_QUERY_DEPENETRATION` |   `3` | verified convex-against-composite correction, not globally minimal |

### `entasis_overlap_state_t`

geometric overlap presence, valid only on an OK status

| Constant                       | Value | Meaning                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ----: | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ENTASIS_OVERLAP_SEPARATED`    |   `0` | no accepted nonnegative-depth geometric contact           |
| `ENTASIS_OVERLAP_INTERSECTING` |   `1` | at least one accepted nonnegative-depth geometric contact |

## Callback types

### `entasis_query_filter_proc_t`

accepts or rejects one complete query candidate

```c
typedef entasis_bool_t (ENTASIS_CALL *entasis_query_filter_proc_t)(void * user_context, entasis_collidable_reference_t collidable);
```

| Parameter      | C type                           | Meaning                                          |
| -------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `user_context` | `void *`                         | caller-owned context passed unchanged by Entasis |
| `collidable`   | `entasis_collidable_reference_t` | target collidable reference                      |

returns ENTASIS_TRUE to keep the candidate or ENTASIS_FALSE to reject it

## Functions

### `entasis_ray`

constructs a world-space ray

direction is not normalized. the hit position is origin + direction * t, so t is a distance only for unit-length directions

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_ray_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_ray(entasis_vector3_t origin, entasis_vector3_t direction, float maximum_t);
```

| Parameter   | C type              | Meaning               |
| ----------- | ------------------- | --------------------- |
| `origin`    | `entasis_vector3_t` | ray origin            |
| `direction` | `entasis_vector3_t` | ray direction         |
| `maximum_t` | `float`             | maximum ray parameter |

returns the ray

### `entasis_ray_cast_any`

reports whether a ray hits any accepted collidable

it uses one stack hit and clips traversal after the first accepted impact

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_ray_cast_any(entasis_world_t * world, entasis_ray_t ray, const entasis_query_filter_t * filter, entasis_bool_t * out_hit, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter    | C type                           | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `world`      | `entasis_world_t *`              | target world                                                                 |
| `ray`        | `entasis_ray_t`                  | ray to execute                                                               |
| `filter`     | `const entasis_query_filter_t *` | query filter applied to candidates                                           |
| `out_hit`    | `entasis_bool_t *`               | receives ENTASIS_TRUE when an accepted hit exists, otherwise ENTASIS_FALSE   |
| `diagnostic` | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`         | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed |

### `entasis_ray_cast_all`

writes ray hits in traversal order

ENTASIS_STATUS_CAPACITY_MISSING reports overflow and out_written identifies the written prefix. results preserve low-level traversal order. this order is not canonical and may change with world topology or implementation details

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_ray_cast_all(entasis_world_t * world, entasis_ray_t ray, const entasis_query_filter_t * filter, entasis_ray_hit_t * hits, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t * out_written, uint64_t * out_required, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter      | C type                           | Meaning                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `world`        | `entasis_world_t *`              | target world                                                                                            |
| `ray`          | `entasis_ray_t`                  | ray to execute                                                                                          |
| `filter`       | `const entasis_query_filter_t *` | query filter applied to candidates                                                                      |
| `hits`         | `entasis_ray_hit_t *`            | caller-owned ray hit output array                                                                       |
| `capacity`     | `uint64_t`                       | number of entries available in the output array                                                         |
| `out_written`  | `uint64_t *`                     | receives the number of output entries written                                                           |
| `out_required` | `uint64_t *`                     | receives out_written on success or the lower bound out_written + 1 on overflow, not the total hit count |
| `diagnostic`   | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`         | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed                            |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK on success or a failure status

### `entasis_query_batch`

publishes query results and observable callbacks in input order. eligible callback-free closest rays use independent per-ray traversal

queries are read-only and add no per-entry C bridge allocation. general queries can grow their existing native scratch pool. all-hit queries write to the caller-owned entasis_query_scratch_t range selected by their entasis_query_output_t, preserving the low-level collector traversal order without canonicalization. every query is attempted. the return value is the first non-OK result status. during a read phase only valid callback-free closest-ray batches on worlds with no active custom shapes are supported. the complete batch is preflighted before result writes. all other batches require a query context

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_query_batch(entasis_world_t * world, const entasis_query_t * queries, uint64_t query_count, entasis_query_result_t * results, uint64_t result_capacity, entasis_query_scratch_t * scratch, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter         | C type                      | Meaning                                                                      |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `world`           | `entasis_world_t *`         | target world                                                                 |
| `queries`         | `const entasis_query_t *`   | input query array                                                            |
| `query_count`     | `uint64_t`                  | number of input queries                                                      |
| `results`         | `entasis_query_result_t *`  | caller-owned result array                                                    |
| `result_capacity` | `uint64_t`                  | number of entries available in the result array                              |
| `scratch`         | `entasis_query_scratch_t *` | caller-owned scratch storage                                                 |
| `diagnostic`      | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`    | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK on success or a failure status

### `entasis_query_context_init`

initializes independent query scratch while the world is idle

a NULL description selects defaults. a borrowed pool is never destroyed and must not be used by any world, worker or other context. the context remains attached until destroyed, preventing world destruction. capacity reservation is not a hard no-growth guarantee


| `query_context` | `entasis_query_context_t *`                   | caller-exclusive context handle                                                    |
| `world`         | `entasis_world_t *`                           | live world kept at a stable address until every context is destroyed               |
| `description`   | `const entasis_query_context_description_t *` | context capacity hints                                                             |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK on success or a failure status

### `entasis_query_context_ray_cast_any`

executes ray cast any with caller-exclusive private query scratch

uses independent collision/traversal scratch, preserving ordinary result and callback semantics. supported during a read phase with one context and independent outputs per caller, or against an idle world. rejects same-context callback reentry. no cross-call callback ordering is promised. the context and callback-local data must not outlive their owner. queries may grow only their private pool when reserved capacity is insufficient
